label: Decisions from logged data with off-policy evaluation
summary: A runnable reference for choosing actions (offers, prices, notifications, routes, treatments) from logged decisions: a reward model, a learned policy, and four offline estimators compared with the hidden true value of each policy.
runtime: Python 3.11+ with numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, scipy and pytest (about 3 seconds)
run: python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt
expected: make_data.py prints 30,000 logged decisions with a reward rate near 33%. baseline.py reports the true value of the best constant action 0.43 and of the learned policy 0.73; the matched-rows estimate says 0.35 and 0.68, inverse-propensity weighting 0.41 and 0.70, self-normalised 0.41 and 0.72 and doubly robust 0.42 and 0.73. pytest reports 5 passed.

files.purpose: A contextual bandit with hidden reward probabilities, a biased logging policy and logged propensities
Reward models, a learned policy and the naive, IPS, SNIPS and doubly robust estimators against the true value
Executable gates: determinism, unbiasedness under random logging, bias of matching, ranking and closeness to the truth

synthetic.description: 30,000 logged decisions with 5 context features and 4 actions. A hidden logistic model gives each action's reward probability; the logging policy favours different actions in different contexts and records the probability with which it chose each action.
knobs: n, logging_temperature: size and how biased the logger is (a very high temperature makes it uniform)
D and K in the file: context features and actions
seed: identical seed gives an identical log

slots.meaning: what is known about the situation when the decision is made
the option chosen: offer, price, route or treatment
the probability with which the logging policy chose that action
predicted reward for each action in each context
the rule that maps context to action

data.threshold: pytest -k deterministic passes; every logged propensity is above 0 and each row's action probabilities sum to 1.0 (tolerance 1e-9)
data.how: Run pytest in the kit directory

features.threshold: Inverse-propensity weighting equals the true value within 0.02 when the logger is uniformly random (60,000 rows)

baseline.threshold: Averaging reward over rows where the logger matched the policy is further from the truth than self-normalised weighting (the kit: error 0.08 against 0.02)

challenger.threshold: Learned policy true value at least 0.2 above the best constant action and a doubly robust estimate within 0.03 of the truth for both policies (the kit: 0.73 against 0.43, errors under 0.01)

tests.pass: Every row has a positive propensity and the action probabilities sum to one
IPS equals the true value within 0.02
Naive error exceeds self-normalised error by more than 0.02

tests.test: Doubly robust is closest to the truth
tests.pass: Within 0.03 of the true value and closer than the naive estimate

lessons.trap: Evaluating a new policy on the rows where it agrees with the old one
lessons.evidence: The matched-rows estimate says 0.35 for a policy worth 0.43 and 0.68 for one worth 0.73, and only 14-16% of rows match.
Without the probability of the logged action no unbiased estimate is possible; the kit stores it on every row.
Inverse-propensity weighting is unbiased but a smallest propensity of 0.0008 makes it noisy; self-normalising and doubly robust estimates are closer.

lessons.trap: Shipping a policy that only looks better offline
lessons.evidence: The learned policy's true value is 0.73 against 0.43 for the best constant, and the doubly robust estimate agrees; this is the check to run before any online test.

target: The reward is 1 if the chosen action succeeded and 0 otherwise. For every logged row the action, its reward and the probability of choosing it are recorded; only the chosen action's reward is observed.
